root_cause.text: In the ublk recovery/fetch path, the per-IO `UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED` bit was only cleared when the entire queue became fully ready, so a partially fetched queue could leave some fetched `struct ublk_io` entries permanently marked canceled and block `ublk_cancel_cmd()` from completing them with `io_uring_cmd_done()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves cancel-flag clearing from `ublk_queue_reset_io_flags()` (which only resets `canceling` and no longer loops over `ubq->ios[j].flags`) into a new `ublk_reset_io_flags(ubq, io)` called from `ublk_mark_io_ready(ub, q_id, io)` on each individual fetch; the CVE text explicitly says the flags “for all IOs in a queue are reset together only once all IOs for that queue have been fetched,” and that this prevented cancellation when only a proper subset of IOs had been fetched.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear the canceled flag per I/O during readiness handling instead of resetting every queued I/O.
intent_record.what: A new helper function `ublk_reset_io_flags(struct ublk_queue *ubq, struct ublk_io *io)` was added to clear `UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED` on a single I/O under `cancel_lock`. The existing `ublk_queue_reset_io_flags()` function was simplified to stop iterating over all `ubq->ios[]` entries and now only clears `ubq->canceling` under the lock and resets `ubq->fail_io` afterward. The signature of `ublk_mark_io_ready()` was changed to take an additional `struct ublk_io *io` parameter.
intent_record.how: The change shifts cancellation-flag cleanup from a queue-wide operation to a per-I/O operation, allowing an individual I/O's canceled state to be cleared when that I/O becomes ready instead of indiscriminately scanning the whole queue. This reduces unnecessary per-queue flag manipulation and supports the updated readiness path that now has direct access to the specific I/O being marked ready.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reset I/O flags when marking an I/O ready to avoid stale state affecting queue readiness and request handling.
intent_record.what: In `ublk_mark_io_ready(struct ublk_device *ub, u16 q_id)`, a new call to `ublk_reset_io_flags(ubq, io);` was inserted immediately after `ubq->nr_io_ready++;` and before the queue-ready check.
intent_record.how: When an I/O becomes ready, the code now clears the I/O flags for that request before testing whether the queue is fully ready. This changes runtime behavior by ensuring any stale or previously set I/O state is reset at the moment readiness is recorded, preventing old flags from affecting subsequent queue readiness or request handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the current I/O context to `ublk_mark_io_ready` so queue readiness is recorded with the correct request state.
intent_record.what: The call to `ublk_mark_io_ready` in `ublk_fetch()` was changed from `ublk_mark_io_ready(ub, q_id)` to `ublk_mark_io_ready(ub, q_id, io)`, adding the `io` argument to the function invocation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now passes the current `io` context into `ublk_mark_io_ready`, allowing that function to associate the queue-ready transition with a specific I/O object rather than only the device and queue ID. This can enable correct state handling for the fetched request and avoid missing per-request information.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the prepared I/O object to `ublk_mark_io_ready()` so readiness can be tracked per I/O instance.
intent_record.what: The call to `ublk_mark_io_ready()` in `ublk_batch_prep_io()` was changed from taking two arguments, `data->ub` and `ubq->q_id`, to taking three arguments by adding `io` as the third parameter.
intent_record.how: When I/O preparation succeeds (`ret == 0`), the code now passes the specific `io` object into `ublk_mark_io_ready()`, allowing that function to associate readiness with the concrete I/O instance instead of only the ub/block queue pair.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the recovery/fetch path and the fix directly. The vulnerable construct was that per-IO canceled state was only cleared in the old device-wide reset path: previously `ublk_reset_io_flags(struct ublk_device *ub)` cleared `UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED` only when `if (ublk_dev_ready(ub)) { ... ublk_reset_io_flags(ub); }`, i.e. only after all queues were ready. That matches the root cause where partially fetched queues could leave some `struct ublk_io` entries canceled. In this commit, the fix is present: the code adds per-queue readiness tracking (`ubq->nr_io_ready`, `ub->nr_queue_ready`) and calls `ublk_queue_reset_io_flags(ubq)` as soon as `if (ublk_queue_ready(ubq))` becomes true, with the comment `Reset queue flags as soon as this queue is ready. This clears the canceling flag, allowing batch FETCH commands to succeed during recovery without waiting for all queues.` It also clears `ubq->canceling = false;` in the per-queue reset. So the vulnerable behavior is present in the pre-fix logic shown in the diff context, but the code in this commit already contains the fix.
